Retrieved 2026-07-20 via Exa web_fetch. ISW (latest daily assessment, dated July 19, published morning of July 20 BST).

TOPLINE: Russian forces conducted one of their LARGEST ballistic missile strikes of the war on the night of 18-19 July, predominantly targeting Kyiv Oblast. Ukrainian Air Force: Russia launched 40 missiles overnight (incl. 10 Zirkon anti-ship, 25 Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic, 3 Onyx, 3 Kh-59/69) plus 125 Shahed/Gerbera/Italmas drones and decoys. Ukraine downed 108 drones, 17 ballistic/Zirkon/S-400 missiles, 1 cruise missile. 23 missiles and 10 drones struck 20 locations. Zelensky: one of the largest ballistic strike packages against Kyiv Oblast since 2022; at least one civilian killed, 16 injured. Zelensky said Russia had been stockpiling missiles for several days for the strike.

Russia has launched MORE ballistic missiles at Ukraine in July than it produces monthly. Militarnyi: Russia used up to two-thirds of its planned ANNUAL Zirkon production in July 2026 alone. July so far: 107 ballistic missiles + 20 Zirkon launched. Russia dipping into stockpiles; exploiting global Patriot interceptor shortages. Drones DOWN: 2,955 in July so far vs 5,749 in June.

Nova Poshta (postal service): Russian forces struck a sorting terminal in Kharkiv Oblast, killing three civilians.

Ukrainian long-range campaign: SBU struck shadow-fleet tanker Avero in Black Sea (one of four struck 10-19 July). USF cmdr "Magyar" Brovdi: Ukrainian forces struck 176 Russian vessels in Black Sea/Azov 6-19 July; destroyed five ferries (responsible for ~80% of military transport from Kavkaz to occupied Crimea), degraded Kerch ferry capacity by 75%. SBU struck three oil depots in Stavropol Krai (~600km from border), large fires. Caspian Pipeline Consortium: Ukrainian drones struck maritime terminal at Novorossiysk, halting oil loading.

KEY TAKEAWAYS: (1) Ukrainian long-range strike campaign against Russian oil/energy infrastructure and naval vessels continued 18-19 July. (2) Russian forces recently advanced in northern Sumy Oblast. Ukrainian forces likely liberated Novopavlivka; advanced 9-10km in places in Novopavlivka/Oleksandrivka directions.

Zelensky reshuffle fallout: Zelensky said 18 July he spoke with both C-in-C Syrskyi and former defence minister Fedorov; aware of communication issues between army and other structures; "decisions regarding the army will be worked out."
